items.title: Rebecca Kilgore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: It’s a tune called “The Duke” by Dave Brubeck. And I’ve just always loved it instrumentally.

ctx.x: Now in a situation like this weekend, where unfortunately Dave [Frishberg] wasn’t here — and we hope he’s all right by the way — was it a little anxious for you to — okay we’re re-working the schedule and now you’re singing with this, and now you’re going to do this and that.

Sure. Because Dave and I have a rapport after having worked together for so long, like five and a half years, and I know a lot of obscure songs. That’s kind of what I gravitate to. I don’t do a lot of standards, which sometimes is a disadvantage. So he and I do these obscure songs and we kind of have these arrangements worked out, and I thought oh boy, this will be fun to pull out some of our strange material and kind of bring something new and different. And well that’s out the window, because a lot of these…

Well I heard you last night. I guess you were singing with Keith [Ingham]. And it got to the end of the tune and you did something that was very musical to do — and I’m not even sure I can describe it, but it just had something to do with when you were going to tag, that you made it obvious, you sang an obvious note so that he knew, okay tag. And then when you got to the very end you just held this note out and let him, and he did kind of his [scats]. But you just held that thing out there, and it sounded like it…
